ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Suppose the isotherm distribution of a certain sea area is as shown in the figure. <image1> According to this figure, in which hemisphere is this sea area located?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the isotherms are generally distributed in an east-west curving pattern. An isotherm in the upper part of the figure is labeled 18℃, and an isotherm in the lower part of the figure is labeled 17℃; according to conventional map orientation, the upper part represents the north side and the lower part represents the south side, so the water temperature on the north side of this sea area is higher than that on the south side. Then reason: Sea water temperature generally decreases from low latitudes near the equator toward the high-latitude poles, and the warmer side points toward the equator. In the figure, the warmer 18℃ is located on the north side, indicating that the equator direction is north of this sea area, so this sea area is located in the Southern Hemisphere.
